name: ocr_assist
description:
Language description:
Read text from the selected image and return both text and an OCR visualization.

Real helper:
_call_ocr_assist(image_index=None, image_obj=None, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- ocr["text"]: OCR text result
- ocr["image"]: OCR visualization image
- ocr["images"]: returned image list
- ocr["meta"]: structured OCR metadata

Short example:
ocr = _call_ocr_assist()
print(ocr.get("text", ""))
result = ocr["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_ocr_assist` for text-heavy images, small text, dense labels, forms, documents, and charts with hard-to-read labels. Treat OCR as an evidence observation to combine with the visible image context when spatial layout, color, ordering, or relations matter.

name: rotate_image
description:
Language description:
Rotate the current image to correct orientation or align the target for easier reading.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL rotation directly.

Short example:
result = image.rotate(90, expand=True)
usage_notes: Use this when the image, chart, document, or label is clearly misoriented. Keep expand=True so the rotated image is not clipped.

name: flip_image
description:
Language description:
Flip the current image horizontally or vertically when the scene is mirrored or upside down.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL transpose operations directly.

Short example:
result = image.transpose(Image.FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT)
usage_notes: Use this when text, axes, or object layout indicates the image is mirrored or upside down.

name: resize_image
description:
Language description:
Resize the current image to enlarge a small target or normalize it before inspection.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; resize directly with PIL.

Short example:
width, height = image.size
result = image.resize((width * 2, height * 2))
usage_notes: Use this when the whole image or crop is too small to inspect comfortably. Keep the resized output as the new working image.

name: adjust_brightness
description:
Language description:
Adjust image brightness to reveal dark or washed-out details.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use ImageEnhance.Brightness directly.

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Brightness(image).enhance(1.4)
usage_notes: Use moderate factors first. Prefer this when task-relevant text or boundaries are hard to see because the image is too dark or washed out.

name: adjust_contrast
description:
Language description:
Adjust image contrast to make faint text, boundaries, or local structure easier to inspect.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use ImageEnhance.Contrast directly.

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Contrast(image).enhance(1.6)
usage_notes: Use moderate factors such as 1.2 to 2.0. Use this when contrast is expected to reveal task-relevant evidence, not as a generic repeated cleanup step.

name: adjust_sharpness
description:
Language description:
Adjust image sharpness to make fine text or edges more legible.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use ImageEnhance.Sharpness directly.

Short example:
result = ImageEnhance.Sharpness(image).enhance(1.6)
usage_notes: Use this when the selected image or crop is slightly blurry or soft. Prefer moderate sharpening over aggressive artifacts.

name: draw_horizontal_line
description:
Language description:
Draw a horizontal reference line at a specified image row to verify chart thresholds, gridline alignment, or whether points are above or below a value.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL ImageDraw directly. The height location must be a pixel y-coordinate in the current rendered image, not a chart-axis value. Work on a copy and assign it to `result`.

Short example:
vis = image.copy()
w, h = vis.size
y = 180
ImageDraw.Draw(vis).line([(0, y), (w, y)], fill="red", width=3)
result = vis
usage_notes: Use this when a row-level visual guide helps compare chart points against a threshold or gridline. Coordinates are pixel coordinates in the selected input image. Keep the line task-relevant and explain what threshold or alignment it is meant to verify.

name: draw_vertical_line
description:
Language description:
Draw a vertical reference line at a specified image column to align chart points with x-axis ticks, categories, or time labels.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL ImageDraw directly. The width location must be a pixel x-coordinate in the current rendered image, not a chart-axis value. Work on a copy and assign it to `result`.

Short example:
vis = image.copy()
w, h = vis.size
x = 240
ImageDraw.Draw(vis).line([(x, 0), (x, h)], fill="red", width=3)
result = vis
usage_notes: Use this when a column-level visual guide helps bind a data point to an x-axis tick, category, or vertical gridline. Coordinates are pixel coordinates in the selected input image. Keep the line task-relevant and explain what tick or point it is meant to verify.

name: draw_point
description:
Language description:
Mark one or more explicit points on the image to identify chart data points, extrema, intersections, object centers, or count candidates.

Direct code capability:
No helper is required; use PIL ImageDraw directly. Each point must be an [x, y] pixel coordinate in the current rendered image, not chart-axis units. Work on a copy and assign it to `result`.

Short example:
vis = image.copy()
d = ImageDraw.Draw(vis)
for x, y in [(120, 180), (180, 150), (240, 130)]:
    r = 5
    d.ellipse((x-r, y-r, x+r, y+r), outline="red", width=3)
result = vis
usage_notes: Use this when sparse markers help preserve exact visual evidence, such as the highest point in a line chart, a threshold-crossing point, or objects being counted. Coordinates are pixel coordinates in the selected input image. Keep markers sparse and task-relevant.

name: manual_box
description:
Language description:
Draw a box on an image using explicit pixel coordinates.

Real helper:
_call_manual_box(x1, y1, x2, y2, image_index=None, image_obj=None, outline="lime", width=2, label=None, label_fill=None)

Key outputs:
- box["image"]: boxed visualization image
- box["meta"]: box metadata

Short example:
box = _call_manual_box(120, 80, 260, 180, label="target")
result = box["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_box` when exact coordinates are already known and marking the region helps verification. Coordinates are pixel coordinates on the selected input image.

name: manual_crop
description:
Language description:
Crop a local region using explicit pixel coordinates.

Real helper:
_call_manual_crop(x1, y1, x2, y2, image_index=None, image_obj=None, padding=0)

Key outputs:
- crop["image"]: cropped image
- crop["meta"]["crop_box"]: clipped crop coordinates

Short example:
crop = _call_manual_crop(120, 80, 260, 180, padding=4)
result = crop["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_crop` when a known local region needs a closer view. Coordinates are pixel coordinates on the selected input image.

name: ground_box
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return a boxed image.

Real helper:
_call_ground_box(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- box["image"]: grounded box visualization image
- box["text"]: helper feedback
- box["meta"]: grounding metadata

Short example:
box = _call_ground_box("price tag")
result = box["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_ground_box` for short visual target phrases. Long prompts or relation-heavy descriptions can make grounding unstable.

name: sam_mask
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return a highlighted SAM2 mask image.

Real helper:
_call_sam_mask(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, multimask_output=False, mask_alpha=0.45, draw_box_on_mask=True, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- mask["image"]: mask visualization image
- mask["text"]: helper feedback
- mask["meta"]: mask metadata

Short example:
mask = _call_sam_mask("hanging tag", multimask_output=False)
result = mask["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_sam_mask` when a highlighted mask helps inspect a target region. Short target phrases work best.

name: dino_crop
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target and return one or more cropped regions.

Real helper:
_call_dino_crop(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, based_on="box", detection_index=0, max_crops=1, padding=0, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, multimask_output=False, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- crop["image"]: primary crop image
- crop["images"]: all returned crop images
- crop["text"]: helper feedback
- crop["meta"]: crop metadata

Short example:
crop = _call_dino_crop("serial number", max_crops=1, padding=4)
result = crop["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_dino_crop` when automatic object-focused cropping from a short text description is likely to isolate relevant evidence. If multiple crops are returned, the final result must still be a single image.

name: blur_bg
description:
Language description:
Keep a grounded target clearer while blurring the background.

Real helper:
_call_blur_bg(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, blur_radius=8.0, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, multimask_output=False, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- focus["image"]: background-blurred image
- focus["text"]: helper feedback
- focus["meta"]: blur metadata

Short example:
focus = _call_blur_bg("label")
result = focus["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_blur_bg` when suppressing background clutter is expected to help inspect the foreground target.

name: manual_depth
description:
Language description:
Measure the depth of an explicit pixel region on the full image.

Real helper:
_call_manual_depth(x1, y1, x2, y2, image_index=None, image_obj=None, stat="median", vis_mode="overlay", padding=0, label=None, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- depth["image"]: full-image visualization with region and depth label
- depth["text"]: depth conclusion
- depth["meta"]: structured depth statistics

Short example:
depth = _call_manual_depth(120, 80, 260, 180, stat="median", label="target")
print(depth["text"])
result = depth["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_manual_depth` when coordinates are known and a stable region-depth estimate is needed.

name: ground_depth
description:
Language description:
Ground a text-described target, pick one detection, then measure that detection region's depth on the full image.

Real helper:
_call_ground_depth(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, detection_index=0, box_threshold=0.35, text_threshold=0.25, stat="median", vis_mode="overlay", padding=0, label=None, **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- depth["image"]: full-image visualization with selected detection and depth label
- depth["text"]: grounding plus depth conclusion
- depth["meta"]: selected detection and depth statistics

Short example:
depth = _call_ground_depth("person", detection_index=0, stat="median")
print(depth["text"])
result = depth["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_ground_depth` when target location is unknown and a single grounded detection plus depth measurement is needed.

name: count_assist
description:
Language description:
Count text-described instances in the selected image and return a count visualization.

Real helper:
_call_count_assist(text_prompt, image_index=None, image_obj=None, confidence_thresh=0.23, visualize="heatmap", **kwargs)

Key outputs:
- count["image"]: count visualization image
- count["text"]: helper feedback
- count["meta"]["count"]: predicted count when available
- count["meta"]: structured count metadata

Short example:
count = _call_count_assist("car", confidence_thresh=0.23, visualize="heatmap")
print(count["meta"].get("count"))
result = count["image"]
usage_notes: Use `_call_count_assist` when the task is to estimate how many instances of a described visual category appear in the image.
